subject: Gateway fabric and control-plane alignment for ACME on-prem VPC
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
To: Tom Baker <tom.baker@acme-corp.com>, Purchasing <purchasing@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 05 Apr 2028 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Gateway fabric and control-plane alignment for ACME on-prem VPC

Hi Tom / ACME team,

Thanks again for the walkthrough this morning. Per our discussion, I wanted to consolidate the open alignment items so we have a single artifact to iterate on before the on-site cutover. High level: ACME will run the data plane (edge gateways + tenant routing) in your colo; Redwood will manage the control plane that performs lifecycle, telemetry aggregation, and rollout coordination. We need to lock the handoff surface between the two and agree SLAs for failover paths.

Key items I want to cover in this thread (short, actionable):
- Gateway fabric binding model (static routes vs BGP peering) — which you prefer for tenant segmentation?
- Control plane ingress egress (TLS termination point, mutual TLS requirements, cert rotation windows)
- Heartbeat and health-check channels (port, protocol, and expected timeouts)
- Observability hooks (what metrics/traces we can pull vs what you will push)
- Cutover plan and canary window for tenant traffic (duration, rollback criteria)

Can you attach the latest gateway spec and any diagrams representing the fabric? I attached a short note on Redwood control-plane constraints so you have our starting point.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Senior Partnerships Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments:
- redwood-controlplane-constraints.md (text)
From: Tom Baker <tom.baker@acme-corp.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
Cc: Purchasing <purchasing@acme-corp.com>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 05 Apr 2028 11:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Gateway fabric and control-plane alignment for ACME on-prem VPC

Naomi — thanks for the clear summary. Attaching the gateway spec and a diagram (GW Fabric v2) that shows our current topology. A few quick notes up front:

- We prefer BGP peering for tenant routes where possible; it simplifies large numbers of prefixes and supports faster failover across our spine. For smaller tenants we can do static route maps.
- TLS: we terminate TLS at the gateway for north-south client traffic; for control plane calls from Redwood we can terminate mTLS at a dedicated management VLAN and present a leaf cert. We'll need CA trust exchange.
- Heartbeat: we run a UDP-based probe on port 5421 with a 5s probe interval and a 20s failure window; we can mirror to a TCP health push if you need stronger guarantees.

Attached: acme-edge-gateway-specs.xlsx; gw-fabric-v2-diagram.pdf

Let us know if the diagram maps to the control-plane endpoints you're planning to expose.

—Tom
Tom Baker
Sr. Network Architect, ACME Infrastructure

Attachments:
- acme-edge-gateway-specs.xlsx (spreadsheet)
- gw-fabric-v2-diagram.pdf (pdf)
From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>, Tom Baker <tom.baker@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 06 Apr 2028 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Gateway fabric and control-plane alignment for ACME on-prem VPC

Tom / team — reviewed the attachments, thanks. A few clarifying questions and proposals from an architecture standpoint:

1) Control-plane ingress: we would like Redwood to terminate mTLS connections at the control-plane VIPs inside your management VLAN. Proposed cipher/profile and cert rotation cadence in the attached constraints doc is 90 days. Is ACME comfortable with a 90-day window? If not, what cadence do you require?

2) BGP peering: Logan and I agree that BGP is preferable for tenant-scale. Two asks: (a) we need direct ASN mapping per tenant so we can advertise deterministic next-hops, and (b) route filtering at ACME edge to avoid route leaks during canary. Can you share a sample RPS filter set?

3) Health checks: the UDP probe works, but for critical leader-election and KV-sync channels we need an out-of-band TCP health check with 3s polling and a 12s failover to avoid split-brain. Can ACME add that TCP probe on the management VLAN?

4) Observability: we will push a lightweight exporter to the gateway management plane that exposes per-tenant token counters and latency histograms. We need permission to scrape on /metrics and a read-only role for a limited set of endpoints.

Action: If ACME can confirm BGP policies, cert cadence, and TCP probe, we'll draft a one-page handoff matrix and propose a 2-hour canary window for the first 100 tenants.

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Principal Infrastructure Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
To: Tom Baker <tom.baker@acme-corp.com>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 07 Apr 2028 07:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Gateway fabric and control-plane alignment for ACME on-prem VPC

Quick ops notes:

- Cutover plan: propose canary with 10 tenants first, 2-hour window, monitor for packet loss, auth failures, and control-plane backlog. Roll forward if stable for 30m, otherwise rollback.
- Telemetry retention: we will initially set the scrape window to 7d for the canary; if ACME can store longer we can extend.
- Runbook: need a clear IP/ASN map and BGP neighbor credentials in advance. Also need a contact cell for ACME on-call (30m SLA).

Irene: agree about the TCP probe for leader-election channels. If ACME cannot enable that, we need to instrument a faster KV-heartbeat on our side and assume degraded failover.

Tom: can you confirm availability for a 2hr canary on Monday 2028-04-09 between 02:00-08:00 UTC? We'll open INF-2347 and link runbook there.

—Logan
Logan Wright
Operations Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
To: Tom Baker <tom.baker@acme-corp.com>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 07 Apr 2028 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Gateway fabric and control-plane alignment for ACME on-prem VPC

Thanks everyone — summary and next steps: 

Decisions agreed (pending Tom confirmation in reply):
- Use BGP peering for tenant routing at scale; static routes for small tenants as fallback.
- TLS/mTLS: Redwood will connect to control-plane VIPs on ACME management VLAN; target cert rotation 90 days unless ACME requests otherwise.
- Health checks: ACME to enable UDP probe (existing) and add a TCP health probe for leader-election channels on management VLAN; ACME to share port details.
- Observability: ACME to allow read-only /metrics scrape from our exporter; Redwood will limit the metrics to per-tenant counters only.
- Canary window: 2-hour window; initial canary with 10 tenants; rollback criteria: >1% packet loss or >3% auth failures or control-plane backlog > 250ms average processing delay over 10 minutes.

Action items:
1) Tom / ACME: share sample RPS filter, BGP neighbor creds, and confirm TCP probe port and cert cadence by EOD Mon 2028-04-09. (Attachments: gw-fabric-v2-diagram.pdf, acme-edge-gateway-specs.xlsx).
2) Logan / Ops: create INF-2347 runbook and populate with IP/ASN mapping and monitoring playbooks.
3) Irene / Infra: draft the one-page handoff matrix and post to the Drive link below.
4) Naomi / Partnerships: coordinate contractual SLA note with Purchasing (cc'd), include the on-call contact and escalation path.

Related links: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1GWF-fabric-v2-diagram, https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-2347

Please reply all with any corrections; otherwise I will consider these items agreed and we will proceed to scheduling.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Senior Partnerships Manager
Redwood Inference
